artists.biography:
Steve White Trio is a UK acid jazz and jazz pop ensemble led by the legendary drummer Steve White, renowned for his foundational role in The Style Council during the 1980s and his appearances at Live Aid in 1985. White first gained fame playing with Paul Weller at age 17, becoming a permanent member of The Style Council and contributing to hits like "Long Hot Summer" and major solo albums including Stanley Road and Heavy Soul. Beyond his work with Weller, White co-founded The Jazz Renegades, one of the pioneering bands of the Acid Jazz movement, and has performed with notable artists such as The Young Disciples, Galliano, JTQ, Oasis, and The Who. His musical journey also includes collaborations in groups like Trio Valore, The Players, and The Family Silver, showcasing his versatility across jazz, soul, and rock genres.

The Steve White Trio, featuring long-time collaborator Chris Hague on guitar and Joel White on keyboards, marks White’s debut as a bandleader with the album Soul Drums, released on March 20, 2026, under Acid Jazz Records as part of the new "Jazz Sessions" series. The instrumental record pays tribute to White’s jazz roots and filmic influences, blending sixties Hammond organ-led R&B, funk grooves, and soul textures inspired by Graham Bond and Brian Auger. The album includes a reworking of The Style Council’s "My Ever Changing Moods" and the single "Changes," reflecting White’s cinematic approach to composition. With a mid-century inspired sleeve and a lineup that also features saxophonist Steve Beighton on select tracks, Soul Drums celebrates White’s enduring legacy while introducing his new trio to the acid jazz scene.

The trio has embarked on a UK tour in April and May 2026, performing at venues such as Band on the Wall in Manchester, Slay in Glasgow, and Thekla in Bristol, with Matt Deighton providing support on most dates. Their music fuses sixties Hammond soul, funk, and blues with a subtle jazz edge, creating a distinctive sound that honors White’s past while pushing forward into new creative territory. As a drum master and legend of acid jazz, Steve White continues to shape the genre through this trio, blending his rich history with fresh, melodic, and cinematic compositions that resonate with both longtime fans and new audiences.

artists.biography:
Steven Douglas White, born on May 31, 1965, in Bermondsey, South London, is a celebrated English drummer best known for his foundational role in The Style Council. He joined the band at the age of 17 after auditioning for Paul Weller’s new group, where his background in jazz and Latin music, including bossa novas and sambas, secured him the gig. White’s drumming became a defining feature of The Style Council’s sound, characterized by powerful grooves, precision, and a fusion of jazz, funk, and rock influences that helped the band transition from pop to a more sophisticated style. His musicality and ability to play with incredible feel and taste earned him recognition as one of the UK’s finest drummers across any genre.

Beyond The Style Council, White has maintained a long-standing collaboration with Paul Weller on his solo albums and has performed with a diverse array of artists including The Who, Oasis, The James Taylor Quartet, and Ian Dury. His brother, Alan White, is also a renowned drummer who played for Oasis for nine years. White’s career extends into education and leadership, where he serves as a respected clinician and educator in the UK drumming scene. Currently, he is the drummer for Hague & White, a modern soulful trio featuring Chris Hague and Joel White, and has contributed to projects such as the soundtrack for the Netflix series Madame Blanc and the debut album of singer Lucca Mae. White continues to be a highly influential figure, blending his jazz roots with contemporary soul and pop, and remains active in the music industry with new solo work and touring plans.

perplexity.description:
Soul Drums by the Steve White Trio marks the prolific session drummer’s first album as a bandleader, serving as the inaugural release in Acid Jazz Records’ new Jazz Sessions series. Credited to White alongside Chris Hague (guitar) and Joel White (keyboards)—the duo known as Hague & White—the instrumental record is a cinematic tribute to White’s jazz roots, blending soul grooves with filmic influences. The album pays homage to early British, Hammond organ-led R&B from artists like Graham Bond and Brian Auger, while featuring guest saxophonist, horn player, and flutist Steve Beighton. Recorded spontaneously at Fox Den Studios in just two days, the project captures a raw, jazz-like energy with strong melodies and a distinct soulful feel that directly inspired the album’s title.

The nine-track collection includes a mellow, reimagined version of The Style Council’s classic “My Ever Changing Moods,” a fitting tribute to White’s fellow Councillors Paul Weller, Mick Talbot, and Dee C. Lee. The single “Changes” leads the album, which also features tracks like “Camera Obscura,” “Something,” and “When The Tourists Leave.” Released on March 20, 2026, Soul Drums is available on LP, CD, and digitally, with an Acid Jazz-exclusive “Opaque Spring Green” color vinyl edition limited to 500 copies. The album’s midcentury-inspired sleeve and its respectful nods to diverse genres reflect White’s desire to create a spontaneous, melodic work that honors the jazz and soul traditions that shaped his early career.
